        ):
            return None

        telegram_user_id = getattr(
            user,
            "id",
            None,
        )

        chat_type = getattr(
            chat,
            "type",
            None,
        )

        if telegram_user_id is None:
            return None

        # =====================================================
        # HARD TRANSPORT BOUNDARY
        # =====================================================

        if chat_type != "private":
            return None

        # =====================================================
        # MESSAGE VALIDATION
        # =====================================================

        text = getattr(
            message,
            "text",
            None,
        )

        if not isinstance(
            text,
            str,
        ):
            return None

        text = text.strip()

        if not text:
            return None

        # =====================================================
        # BETA ACCESS AUTHORIZATION
        # =====================================================

        try:
            authorized = await (
                self._private_chat_gate.authorize(
                    telegram_user_id=telegram_user_id,
                    chat_type=chat_type,
                )
            )

        except Exception:
            logger.exception(
                "Telegram private-chat authorization failed."
            )

            await self._reply(
                message,
                (
                    "We could not verify your "
                    "EasyChatBot Academy access. "
                    "Please try again."
                ),
            )

            return None

        if not authorized:
            await self._reply(
                message,
                (
                    "Your EasyChatBot Academy Telegram "
                    "access is not authorized and is not "
                    "approved for Beta access."
                ),
            )

            return None

        # =====================================================
        # CONVERSATION BOUNDARY
        # =====================================================

        try:
            response = await (
                self._conversation_boundary.handle_message(
                    telegram_user_id=telegram_user_id,
                    message=text,
                )
            )

        except Exception:
            logger.exception(
                "Telegram classroom conversation processing failed."
            )

            await self._reply(
                message,
                (
                    "Sorry, I could not process "
                    "your classroom message. "
                    "Please try again."
                ),
            )

            return None

        # =====================================================
        # SINGLE RESPONSE DELIVERY POINT
        # =====================================================

        if (
            isinstance(response, str)
            and response.strip()
        ):
            await self._reply(
                message,
                response,
            )

            # Delivery has already happened exactly once.
            #
            # Return only for observability/testing.
            #
            # The runtime MUST ignore this value.
            return response

        return None

    # =========================================================
    # Helpers
    # =========================================================

    @staticmethod
    def _extract_start_token(
        context: Any,
    ) -> str | None:
        args = getattr(
            context,
            "args",
            None,
        )

        if not args:
            return None

        if not isinstance(
            args,
            (list, tuple),
        ):
            return None

        if not args[0]:
            return None

        return str(
            args[0]
        )

    @staticmethod
    async def _reply(
        message: Any,
        text: str,
    ) -> None:
        if message is None:
            return

        reply_text = getattr(
            message,
            "reply_text",
            None,
        )

        if reply_text is None:
            return

        await reply_text(
            text,
        )


__all__ = [
    "BetaTelegramAdapter",
]

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from ..domain.models import ProjectControlSnapshot, ProjectDefinition, ProjectEvent
from ..domain.ports import (
    ProjectEventRepository,
    ProjectRegistry,
    SnapshotRepository,
)


@dataclass
class InMemoryProjectRegistry(ProjectRegistry):
    projects: dict[str, ProjectDefinition] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def get(self, project_id: str) -> ProjectDefinition | None:
        return self.projects.get(project_id)

    def list_active(self) -> list[ProjectDefinition]:
        return [p for p in self.projects.values() if p.active]

    def save(self, project: ProjectDefinition) -> ProjectDefinition:
        self.projects[project.project_id] = project
        return project


@dataclass
class InMemorySnapshotRepository(SnapshotRepository):
    data: dict[str, list[ProjectControlSnapshot]] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def save(self, snapshot: ProjectControlSnapshot) -> ProjectControlSnapshot:
        self.data.setdefault(snapshot.project_id, []).insert(0, snapshot)
        return snapshot

    def list_for_project(
        self, project_id: str, limit: int = 30
    ) -> list[ProjectControlSnapshot]:
        return self.data.get(project_id, [])[:limit]


@dataclass
class InMemoryProjectEventRepository(ProjectEventRepository):
    data: dict[str, list[ProjectEvent]] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def save(self, event: ProjectEvent) -> ProjectEvent:
        self.data.setdefault(event.project_id, []).insert(0, event)
        return event

    def list_for_project(
        self, project_id: str, limit: int = 100
    ) -> list[ProjectEvent]:
        return self.data.get(project_id, [])[:limit]

@dataclass
class FakeTelegramMessage:

class FakeTelegramClient:
    """Deterministic Telegram transport test double."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.calls: list[dict[str, str]] = []

    async def send_message(
        self,
        *,
        chat_id: str,
        text: str,
        parse_mode: str,
    ) -> FakeTelegramMessage:
        self.calls.append(
            {
                "chat_id": chat_id,
                "text": text,
                "parse_mode": parse_mode,
            }
        )

        return FakeTelegramMessage(message_id=9001)


class InMemoryExecutionRepository:
    """Minimal durable repository double for the integration test."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.records = {}

    async def get_by_idempotency_key(self, idempotency_key: str):
        return self.records.get(idempotency_key)

    async def create_started(
        self,
        *,
        publication_id,
        idempotency_key,
        correlation_id,
    ):
        from datetime import datetime, timezone

        from app.application.announcements.execution.durable_contracts import (
            DurableExecutionStatus,
            PublicationExecutionRecord,
        )

        existing = self.records.get(idempotency_key)

        if existing is not None:
            return existing

        now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)

        record = PublicationExecutionRecord(
            publication_id=publication_id,
            idempotency_key=idempotency_key,
            correlation_id=correlation_id,
            attempt=1,
            status=DurableExecutionStatus.STARTED,
            provider_message_id=None,
            error_code=None,
            created_at=now,
            updated_at=now,
        )

        self.records[idempotency_key] = record
        return record

    async def mark_succeeded(
        self,
        *,
        idempotency_key,
        provider_message_id,
    ):
        from dataclasses import replace
        from datetime import datetime, timezone

        from app.application.announcements.execution.durable_contracts import (
            DurableExecutionStatus,
        )

        record = self.records[idempotency_key]

        updated = replace(
            record,
            status=DurableExecutionStatus.SUCCEEDED,
            provider_message_id=provider_message_id,
            error_code=None,
            updated_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
        )

        self.records[idempotency_key] = updated
        return updated

    async def mark_failed(
        self,
        *,
        idempotency_key,
        error_code,
    ):
        from dataclasses import replace
        from datetime import datetime, timezone

        from app.application.announcements.execution.durable_contracts import (
            DurableExecutionStatus,
        )

        record = self.records[idempotency_key]

        updated = replace(
            record,
            status=DurableExecutionStatus.FAILED,
            error_code=error_code,
            updated_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
        )

        self.records[idempotency_key] = updated
        return updated


class RecordingAudit:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.successes: list[dict] = []
        self.failures: list[dict] = []

    async def record_success(self, **kwargs) -> None:
        self.successes.append(kwargs)

    async def record_failure(self, **kwargs) -> None:
        self.failures.append(kwargs)


@dataclass
class ApprovedPublication:
    id: object
    title: str = "Beta 2"
    content: str = "EasyChatBot Beta 2 is available."
    status: str = "approved"

    def begin_publish(self) -> None:
        pass

    def publish_success(
        self,
        provider_message_id: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.status = "published"

    def mark_failure(self, error_code: str) -> None:
        self.status = "failed"


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_ws22_3_3_executes_through_telegram_adapter() -> None:
    telegram_client = FakeTelegramClient()

    telegram_publisher = TelegramAnnouncementPublisher(
        telegram_client=telegram_client,
    )

    bridge = LegacyAnnouncementPublisherBridge(
        publisher=telegram_publisher,
        channel_id="-100123456789",
    )

    repository = InMemoryExecutionRepository()
    audit = RecordingAudit()

    service = DurablePublicationExecutionService(
        publisher=bridge,
        execution_repository=repository,
        audit=audit,
    )

    publication_id = uuid4()

    request = PublicationExecutionRequest(
        publication_id=publication_id,
        idempotency_key=f"ws22-3-3-{uuid4()}",
        actor="integration-test",
        correlation_id=f"corr-{uuid4()}",
    )

    publication = ApprovedPublication(
        id=publication_id,
    )

    result = await service.execute(
        publication=publication,
        request=request,
    )

    assert result.status is PublicationExecutionStatus.SUCCEEDED
    assert result.provider_message_id == "9001"

    assert len(telegram_client.calls) == 1
    assert telegram_client.calls[0] == {
        "chat_id": "-100123456789",
        "text": (
            "Beta 2\n\n"
            "EasyChatBot Beta 2 is available."
        ),
        "parse_mode": "Markdown",
    }

    persisted = await repository.get_by_idempotency_key(
        request.idempotency_key
    )

    assert persisted is not None
    assert persisted.provider_message_id == "9001"
    assert persisted.correlation_id == request.correlation_id
    assert persisted.publication_id == publication_id

    assert len(audit.successes) == 1
    assert audit.successes[0]["publication_id"] == publication_id
    assert audit.successes[0]["actor"] == "integration-test"
    assert (
        audit.successes[0]["correlation_id"]
        == request.correlation_id
    )
    assert (
        audit.successes[0]["provider_message_id"]
        == "9001"
    )


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_ws22_3_3_idempotency_prevents_second_telegram_send() -> None:
    telegram_client = FakeTelegramClient()

    telegram_publisher = TelegramAnnouncementPublisher(
        telegram_client=telegram_client,
    )

    bridge = LegacyAnnouncementPublisherBridge(
        publisher=telegram_publisher,
        channel_id="-100123456789",
    )

    repository = InMemoryExecutionRepository()
    audit = RecordingAudit()

    service = DurablePublicationExecutionService(
        publisher=bridge,
        execution_repository=repository,
        audit=audit,
    )

    publication_id = uuid4()

    request = PublicationExecutionRequest(
        publication_id=publication_id,
        idempotency_key=f"ws22-3-3-idempotent-{uuid4()}",
        actor="integration-test",
        correlation_id=f"corr-{uuid4()}",
    )

    first = await service.execute(
        publication=ApprovedPublication(id=publication_id),
        request=request,
    )

    second = await service.execute(
        publication=ApprovedPublication(id=publication_id),
        request=request,
    )

    assert first.status is PublicationExecutionStatus.SUCCEEDED

    assert (
        second.status
        is PublicationExecutionStatus.IDEMPOTENT_REPLAY
    )

    assert second.provider_message_id == "9001"

    # Critical WS-22 guarantee:
    # the provider receives exactly one publication.
    assert len(telegram_client.calls) == 1

    # Only the original successful execution records an audit success.
    assert len(audit.successes) == 1

)

class FakeProvider(LLMProvider):
    def __init__(self, result: ProviderResult):
        self.result = result

    async def generate(self, *, system_prompt: str, user_message: str):
        return self.result


def _capture():
    repository = InMemoryProviderUsageRepository()
    service = ProviderUsageService(repository)
    return ProviderUsageCapture(service), repository


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_runtime_captures_successful_provider_result():
    capture, repository = _capture()
    result = ProviderResult(
        success=True,
        provider_id="openai",
        model="gpt-5-mini",
        content="Bonjour",
        usage=ProviderUsage(input_tokens=10, output_tokens=5, total_tokens=15),
        provider_request_id="req_test_1",
        latency_ms=120,
    )
    runtime = ConversationRuntime(
        llm_provider=FakeProvider(result),
        usage_capture=capture,
        usage_context=ProviderUsageContext(
            capability="conversation",
            functionality="chat",
            agent="conversation_agent",
            estimated_cost=Decimal("0"),
        ),
    )

    assert await runtime.respond(
        character_instruction="You are a French teacher.",
        learner_message="Bonjour",
    ) == "Bonjour"

    events = repository.get_all()
    assert len(events) == 1
    assert events[0].provider == "openai"
    assert events[0].input_tokens == 10
    assert events[0].output_tokens == 5
    assert events[0].success is True

    calls = []

    class Handler:
        async def handle(self, **kwargs):
            calls.append(kwargs)

    class Gate:
        async def authorize(self, **kwargs):
            return True

    adapter = BetaTelegramAdapter(
        start_handler=Handler(),
        private_chat_gate=Gate(),
    )

    update = FakeUpdate(
        effective_user=FakeUser(111),
        effective_chat=FakeChat(
            111,
            "private",
        ),
        effective_message=FakeMessage(),
    )

    await adapter.handle_start(
        update,
        FakeContext(),
    )

    assert len(calls) == 1

    call = calls[0]

    assert call["token"] is None
    assert call["telegram_user_id"] == 111
    assert call["chat_id"] == 111
    assert call["chat_type"] == "private"

    # Telegram transport owns reply delivery.
    # The adapter passes an explicit reply callback
    # into the start-handler boundary.
    assert "reply" in call
    assert callable(call["reply"])

    *,
    availability: str = "enabled",

    boundary = BetaTelegramConversationBoundary(
        conversation_service=conversation_service,
        beta_access_service=beta_access_service,
        functionality_control_service=control_service,
    )

    return boundary, control_service

def test_telegram_runtime_composition_creates_runtime(
    monkeypatch,
):
    #
    # Test-only privacy configuration.
    #
    # Never use this value as a production secret.
    #
    monkeypatch.setenv(
        "PRIVACY_HASH_SECRET",
        "test-only-telegram-composition-secret",
    )

    #
    # Database dependency isolation.
    #

    class FakeEngine:
        pass

    class FakeSessionFactory:
        pass

    monkeypatch.setattr(
        "backend.application.telegram_bootstrap.create_database_engine",
        lambda: FakeEngine(),
    )

    monkeypatch.setattr(
        "backend.application.telegram_bootstrap.create_session_factory",
        lambda engine: FakeSessionFactory(),
    )

    #
    # AI runtime isolation.
    #

    monkeypatch.setattr(
        "backend.application.telegram_bootstrap.create_conversation_runtime",
        lambda: FakeConversationRuntime(),
    )

    #
    # Functionality-control isolation.
    #
    # The production composition requires this dependency explicitly.
    # The test supplies a deterministic repository-backed service rather
    # than weakening the production contract.
    #

    functionality_control_service = (
        make_functionality_control_service()
    )

    reset_telegram_runtime()

    try:
        runtime = create_telegram_runtime(
            functionality_control_service=(
                functionality_control_service
            ),
            language_detector=DeterministicLanguageDetector(),
        )

        assert runtime is not None

        composition = get_telegram_production_composition()

        assert composition is not None
        assert composition.conversation_boundary is not None

    finally:
        reset_telegram_runtime()

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import replace
from unittest.mock import Mock

import pytest

from app.application.beta_access.telegram_conversation_service import (
    TelegramConversationService,
)
from app.application.uai.language.language_response_policy import (
    LanguageResponsePolicy,
)
from app.application.uai.world.world_resolver import WorldResolver
from app.domain.uai.context.world_context import (
    LanguagePolicy,
    WorldContext,

CANONICAL_WORLD_ID = "french_world"


class FakeLanguageDetector:
    """Deterministic language detector used by service integration tests."""

    def __init__(self, language: str = "fr") -> None:
        self.language = language
        self.calls: list[str] = []

    def detect(self, text: str) -> str:
        self.calls.append(text)
        return self.language


class FakeConversationRuntime:
    """Test double for the AI conversation runtime."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.calls: list[dict] = []

    async def respond(
        self,
        *,
        character_instruction: str,
        learner_message: str,
    ) -> str:
        self.calls.append(
            {
                "character_instruction": character_instruction,
                "learner_message": learner_message,
            }
        )

        return (
            "Bonjour, bienvenue à l'Académie EasyChatBot."
        )


class FakeConversationEventRepository:
    """
    In-memory repository test double.

    Implements the production repository contract:

        telegram_user_hash
                +
        conversation_id
                +
            world_id
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.events: list[object] = []
        self.get_recent_calls: list[dict] = []

    async def save(self, event):
        self.events.append(event)
        return event

    async def get_recent(
        self,
        *,
        telegram_user_hash: str,
        conversation_id: str,
        world_id: str,
        limit: int = 20,
    ):
        self.get_recent_calls.append(
            {
                "telegram_user_hash": telegram_user_hash,
                "conversation_id": conversation_id,
                "world_id": world_id,
                "limit": limit,
            }
        )

        if limit <= 0:
            return []

        matching_events = [
            event
            for event in self.events
            if (
                event.telegram_user_hash
                == telegram_user_hash
                and event.conversation_id
                == conversation_id
                and event.world_id
                == world_id
            )
        ]

        return matching_events[-limit:]


class FakePrivacyIdentifierService:
    """Deterministic pseudonymisation test double."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.calls: list[str] = []

    def pseudonymize_identifier(
        self,
        identifier: str,
    ) -> str:
        self.calls.append(identifier)

        return f"hash-{identifier}"


class FakeConversationEventValidator:
    """Test double for conversation governance validation."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.calls: list[dict] = []

    def validate(
        self,
        *,
        content: str,
        metadata: dict,
        telegram_user_hash: str,
    ) -> dict:
        self.calls.append(
            {
                "content": content,
                "metadata": metadata,
                "telegram_user_hash": telegram_user_hash,
            }
        )

        if not telegram_user_hash:
            raise ValueError(
                "Conversation event requires pseudonymous identity."
            )

        if not content:
            raise ValueError(
                "Conversation content cannot be empty."
            )

        if metadata is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "Conversation metadata missing."
            )

        return {
            "valid": True,
        }


def make_service(
    *,
    world_id: str = CANONICAL_WORLD_ID,
    world_name: str = "French World",
    language_code: str | None = "fr",
    world_type: str = "language",
    learning_domain: str | None = "language_learning",
    detected_language: str = "fr",
):
    runtime = FakeConversationRuntime()
    repository = FakeConversationEventRepository()
    privacy = FakePrivacyIdentifierService()
    validator = FakeConversationEventValidator()
    detector = FakeLanguageDetector(detected_language)

    if world_type == "language":
        language_policy = LanguagePolicy(
            mode="target_language",
            target_language=language_code,
        )
    else:
        language_policy = LanguagePolicy(
            mode="mirror_user",
            supported_languages=(
                "en",
                "fr",
                "es",
                "pl",
                "de",
                "it",
                "pt",
                "ru",
                "zh",
                "ar",
            ),
        )

    world = WorldContext(
        world_id=world_id,
        name=world_name,
        language_code=language_code,
        available_characters=("yeti", "alix"),
        world_type=world_type,
        learning_domain=learning_domain,
        language_policy=language_policy,
    )

    class FakeWorldRepository:
        def get_by_id(self, requested_world_id: str):
            if requested_world_id == world_id:
                return world
            return None

    world_resolver = Mock(spec=WorldResolver)
    world_resolver.resolve.return_value = world

    service = TelegramConversationService(
        conversation_runtime=runtime,
        conversation_event_repository=repository,
        privacy_identifier_service=privacy,
        conversation_event_validator=validator,
        language_response_policy=LanguageResponsePolicy(),
        language_detector=detector,
        world_resolver=world_resolver,
    )

    return (
        service,
        runtime,
        repository,
        privacy,
        validator,
        detector,
    )


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_telegram_conversation_service_delegates_to_runtime():
    (
        service,
        runtime,
        repository,
        privacy,
        validator,
        detector,
    ) = make_service()

    response = await service.handle_telegram_message(
        telegram_user_id=12345,
        message="Bonjour",
    )

    assert response == (
        "Bonjour, bienvenue à l'Académie EasyChatBot."
    )

    assert len(runtime.calls) == 1

    assert runtime.calls[0]["learner_message"] == (
        "Bonjour"
    )

    assert "EasyChatBot Academy" in (
        runtime.calls[0]["character_instruction"]
    )

    assert privacy.calls == [
        "12345",
    ]

    assert len(repository.events) == 2

    assert repository.events[0].role == "user"
    assert repository.events[0].content == "Bonjour"
    assert repository.events[0].world_id == CANONICAL_WORLD_ID

    assert repository.events[1].role == "assistant"
    assert repository.events[1].content == response
    assert repository.events[1].world_id == CANONICAL_WORLD_ID

    assert len(validator.calls) == 2

    assert validator.calls[0]["content"] == "Bonjour"
    assert validator.calls[1]["content"] == response

    assert (
        validator.calls[0]["telegram_user_hash"]
        == "hash-12345"
    )

async def test_telegram_conversation_service_retrieves_recent_history():

        "telegram-"
    )

    assert latest_call["limit"] > 0

    # The second turn must retrieve the first turn's history.
    assert len(repository.events) == 4

    assert runtime.calls[-1]["learner_message"] == (
        "Comment allez-vous ?"
    )

async def test_telegram_conversation_service_history_isolated_by_identity():
    (
        service,
        runtime,
        repository,
        privacy,
        validator,
        detector,
    ) = make_service()

    await service.handle_telegram_message(
        telegram_user_id=12345,
        message="David message",
    )

    await service.handle_telegram_message(
        telegram_user_id=67890,
        message="Brother message",
    )

    david_events = await repository.get_recent(
        telegram_user_hash="hash-12345",
        conversation_id=(
            repository.events[0].conversation_id
        ),
        world_id=CANONICAL_WORLD_ID,
    )

    brother_events = await repository.get_recent(
        telegram_user_hash="hash-67890",
        conversation_id=(
            repository.events[2].conversation_id
        ),
        world_id=CANONICAL_WORLD_ID,
    )

    assert david_events
    assert brother_events

    assert all(
        event.telegram_user_hash == "hash-12345"
        for event in david_events
    )

    assert all(
        event.telegram_user_hash == "hash-67890"
        for event in brother_events
    )

    assert not any(
        event.content == "Brother message"
        for event in david_events
    )

    assert not any(
        event.content == "David message"
        for event in brother_events
    )

    assert all(
        event.conversation_id == second_conversation_id
        for event in second_history

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

import pytest

from app.infrastructure.telegram.telegram_bot_runtime import (
    TelegramBotRuntime,
)


class FakeAdapter:
    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        conversation_boundary,
    ) -> None:
        self._conversation_boundary = conversation_boundary

    async def handle_start(
        self,
        update,
        context,
    ):
        return None

    async def handle_message(
        self,
        update,
        context,
    ):
        user = update.effective_user
        message = update.effective_message

        if user is None:
            return None

        if message is None:
            return None

        if not message.text:
            return None

        response = await (
            self._conversation_boundary.handle_message(
                telegram_user_id=user.id,
                message=message.text,
            )
        )

        # The real BetaTelegramAdapter owns Telegram response
        # delivery. The fake must model the same contract.
        if (
            isinstance(response, str)
            and response.strip()
        ):
            await message.reply_text(response)

        return response


@dataclass
class FakeUser:
    id: int


@dataclass
class FakeChat:
    id: int
    type: str


class FakeMessage:
    def __init__(
        self,
        text: str | None,
    ) -> None:
        self.text = text
        self.replies: list[str] = []

    async def reply_text(
        self,
        message: str,
    ) -> None:
        self.replies.append(message)


@dataclass
class FakeUpdate:
    effective_user: FakeUser
    effective_chat: FakeChat
    effective_message: FakeMessage


class FakeConversationBoundary:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.calls: list[dict] = []

    async def handle_message(
        self,
        *,
        telegram_user_id: int,
        message: str,
    ) -> str:
        self.calls.append(
            {
                "telegram_user_id": telegram_user_id,
                "message": message,
            }
        )

        return "Private classroom response"


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_private_message_reaches_conversation_boundary():
    boundary = FakeConversationBoundary()

    runtime = TelegramBotRuntime(
        adapter=FakeAdapter(
            conversation_boundary=boundary,
        ),
        conversation_boundary=boundary,
    )

    update = FakeUpdate(
        effective_user=FakeUser(id=111),
        effective_chat=FakeChat(
            id=111,
            type="private",
        ),
        effective_message=FakeMessage(
            "Bonjour",
        ),
    )

    await runtime._handle_private_message(
        update,
        None,
    )

    assert boundary.calls == [
        {
            "telegram_user_id": 111,
            "message": "Bonjour",
        }
    ]

    # The adapter owns Telegram response delivery.
    # The runtime must not send a second response.
    assert update.effective_message.replies == [
        "Private classroom response",
    ]

async def test_empty_message_is_ignored():

from app.application.uai.world.world_resolver import (
    WorldResolver,
)
from app.domain.uai.context.world_context import (
    LanguagePolicy,
    WorldContext,
)


class DeterministicLanguageDetector:
    """
    Deterministic language-detector test double.

    WS04 does not test the language-detection implementation itself.
    It only requires a controlled detector so the real
    TelegramConversationService can execute its M2-E.2 response-language
    policy without an external provider.
    """

    def __init__(self, language: str = "fr") -> None:
        self.language = language
        self.calls: list[str] = []

    def detect(self, text: str) -> str:
        self.calls.append(text)
        return self.language


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FakeConversationContext:
    world_id: str = "world-fr"
    language_code: str = "fr"
    character: str = "Alix"
    level: str = "B1"


class FakeBetaAccessService:
    """Minimal authorization/context boundary for WS-04 tests."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        authorized: bool = True,
    ) -> None:
        self.authorized = authorized
        self.calls: list[int] = []

    async def get_conversation_context(
        self,
        telegram_user_id: int,
    ) -> FakeConversationContext:
        self.calls.append(telegram_user_id)

        if not self.authorized:
            raise PermissionError(
                "Telegram user is not approved."
            )

        return FakeConversationContext()


class FakeConversationRuntime:
    """Deterministic ConversationRuntime test double."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.calls: list[dict[str, str]] = []

    async def respond(
        self,
        *,
        character_instruction: str,
        learner_message: str,
    ) -> str:
        self.calls.append(
            {
                "character_instruction": character_instruction,
                "learner_message": learner_message,
            }
        )

        return (
            "Bonjour ! Continuons notre pratique du français."
        )


class FakeConversationEventRepository:
    """
    In-memory conversation-event repository.

    Implements the production repository isolation contract:

        telegram_user_hash
                +
        conversation_id
                +
              world_id
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.events: list[Any] = []
        self.get_recent_calls: list[dict[str, Any]] = []

    async def save(self, event):
        self.events.append(event)
        return event

    async def get_recent(
        self,
        *,
        telegram_user_hash: str,
        conversation_id: str,
        world_id: str,
        limit: int = 20,
    ):
        self.get_recent_calls.append(
            {
                "telegram_user_hash": telegram_user_hash,
                "conversation_id": conversation_id,
                "world_id": world_id,
                "limit": limit,
            }
        )

        if limit <= 0:
            return []

        events = [
            event
            for event in self.events
            if (
                event.telegram_user_hash
                == telegram_user_hash
                and event.conversation_id
                == conversation_id
                and event.world_id
                == world_id
            )
        ]

        return events[-limit:]


class FakePrivacyIdentifierService:
    """Deterministic privacy service for integration testing."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.calls: list[str] = []

    def pseudonymize_identifier(
        self,
        identifier: str,
    ) -> str:
        self.calls.append(identifier)

        return f"pseudonymous-{identifier}"


class FakeConversationEventValidator:
    """Minimal event governance validator."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.calls: list[dict[str, Any]] = []

    def validate(
        self,
        *,
        content: str,
        metadata: dict[str, Any],
        telegram_user_hash: str,
    ) -> dict[str, bool]:
        self.calls.append(
            {
                "content": content,
                "metadata": metadata,
                "telegram_user_hash": telegram_user_hash,
            }
        )

        if not content.strip():
            raise ValueError(
                "Conversation content cannot be empty."
            )

        if not telegram_user_hash:
            raise ValueError(
                "Conversation event requires pseudonymous identity."
            )

        if metadata is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "Conversation metadata missing."
            )

        return {"valid": True}


def make_conversation_service():
    runtime = FakeConversationRuntime()
    repository = FakeConversationEventRepository()
    privacy = FakePrivacyIdentifierService()
    validator = FakeConversationEventValidator()

    language_response_policy = LanguageResponsePolicy()
    language_detector = DeterministicLanguageDetector("fr")

    world_resolver = MagicMock(
        spec=WorldResolver,
    )

    world_resolver.resolve.return_value = WorldContext(
        world_id="world-fr",
        name="French World",
        language_code="fr",
        available_characters=[
            "yeti",
            "alix",
        ],
        world_type="language",
        learning_domain="language",
        language_policy=LanguagePolicy(
            mode="target_language",
            target_language="fr",
        ),
    )

    service = TelegramConversationService(
        conversation_runtime=runtime,
        conversation_event_repository=repository,
        privacy_identifier_service=privacy,
        conversation_event_validator=validator,
        language_response_policy=language_response_policy,
        language_detector=language_detector,
        world_resolver=world_resolver,
    )

    return (
        service,
        runtime,
        repository,
        privacy,
        validator,
    )


def make_boundary(
    *,
    authorized: bool = True,
):
    (
        conversation_service,
        runtime,
        repository,
        privacy,
        validator,
    ) = make_conversation_service()

    access = FakeBetaAccessService(
        authorized=authorized,
    )

    boundary = BetaTelegramConversationBoundary(
        conversation_service=conversation_service,
        beta_access_service=access,
    )

    return (
        boundary,
        access,
        conversation_service,
        runtime,
        repository,
        privacy,
        validator,
    )


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_ws04_private_classroom_message_completes_full_application_flow():
    (
        boundary,
        access,
        _conversation_service,
        runtime,
        repository,
        privacy,
        validator,
    ) = make_boundary()

    response = await boundary.handle_message(
        telegram_user_id=12345,
        message="Bonjour",
    )

    assert response == (
        "Bonjour ! Continuons notre pratique du français."
    )

    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    # Authorization / context
    # ---------------------------------------------------------

    assert access.calls == [12345]

    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    # Privacy boundary
    # ---------------------------------------------------------

    assert privacy.calls == ["12345"]

    assert all(
        event.telegram_user_hash == "pseudonymous-12345"
        for event in repository.events
    )

    # Raw Telegram identity must never become an event identity.
    assert all(
        event.telegram_user_hash != "12345"
        for event in repository.events
    )

    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    # Conversation events
    # ---------------------------------------------------------

    assert len(repository.events) == 2

    user_event = repository.events[0]
    assistant_event = repository.events[1]

    assert user_event.role == "user"
    assert user_event.content == "Bonjour"

    assert assistant_event.role == "assistant"
    assert assistant_event.content == response

    assert user_event.channel == "telegram"
    assert assistant_event.channel == "telegram"

    assert user_event.world_id == "world-fr"
    assert assistant_event.world_id == "world-fr"

    assert user_event.conversation_id == (
        assistant_event.conversation_id
    )

    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    # Conversation retrieval
    # ---------------------------------------------------------

    assert len(repository.get_recent_calls) == 1

    retrieval = repository.get_recent_calls[0]

    assert retrieval["telegram_user_hash"] == (
        "pseudonymous-12345"
    )

    assert retrieval["conversation_id"] == (
        user_event.conversation_id
    )

    assert retrieval["world_id"] == "world-fr"

    assert retrieval["limit"] == (
        _conversation_service.HISTORY_LIMIT
    )

    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    # Governance validation
    # ---------------------------------------------------------

    assert len(validator.calls) == 2

    assert validator.calls[0]["content"] == "Bonjour"
    assert validator.calls[1]["content"] == response

    assert (
        validator.calls[0]["telegram_user_hash"]
        == "pseudonymous-12345"
    )

    assert (
        validator.calls[1]["telegram_user_hash"]
        == "pseudonymous-12345"
    )

    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    # Runtime execution
    # ---------------------------------------------------------

    assert len(runtime.calls) == 1

    assert runtime.calls[0]["learner_message"] == "Bonjour"

    assert (
        "EasyChatBot Academy"
        in runtime.calls[0]["character_instruction"]
    )

    assert (
        "Learning language: fr"
        in runtime.calls[0]["character_instruction"]
    )

    assert validator.calls == []

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

import pytest

from app.application.beta_access.beta_telegram_conversation_boundary import (
    BetaTelegramConversationBoundary,
)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FakeConversationContext:
    world_id: str = "world-fr"
    character: str = "Alix"
    level: str = "B1"


class FakeBetaAccessService:
    """Deterministic authorization/context test double."""

    def __init__(self, *, approved: bool = True) -> None:
        self.approved = approved
        self.calls: list[int] = []

    async def get_conversation_context(
        self,
        telegram_user_id: int,
    ) -> FakeConversationContext:
        self.calls.append(telegram_user_id)

        if not self.approved:
            raise PermissionError(
                "Telegram user is not approved."
            )

        return FakeConversationContext()


class FakeConversationService:
    """Deterministic conversation-service test double."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        response: str = "Bonjour !",
        error: Exception | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.response = response
        self.error = error
        self.calls: list[dict] = []

    async def handle_telegram_message(
        self,
        *,
        telegram_user_id: int,
        message: str,
    ) -> str:
        self.calls.append(
            {
                "telegram_user_id": telegram_user_id,
                "message": message,
            }
        )

        if self.error is not None:
            raise self.error

        return self.response


def make_boundary(
    *,
    approved: bool = True,
    conversation_error: Exception | None = None,
):
    access = FakeBetaAccessService(
        approved=approved,
    )

    conversation_service = FakeConversationService(
        error=conversation_error,
    )

    boundary = BetaTelegramConversationBoundary(
        conversation_service=conversation_service,
        beta_access_service=access,
    )

    return (
        boundary,
        access,
        conversation_service,
    )

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

import pytest

from app.application.beta_access.beta_telegram_conversation_boundary import (
    BetaTelegramConversationBoundary,
)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FakeConversationContext:
    world_id: str = "world-fr"
    character: str = "Alix"
    level: str = "B1"


class FakeBetaAccessService:
    """Deterministic Beta authorization boundary."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        approved_users: set[int] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.approved_users = (
            approved_users
            if approved_users is not None
            else {111, 222}
        )

        self.calls: list[int] = []

    async def get_conversation_context(
        self,
        telegram_user_id: int,
    ) -> FakeConversationContext:
        self.calls.append(
            telegram_user_id,
        )

        if telegram_user_id not in self.approved_users:
            raise PermissionError(
                "Telegram user is not approved."
            )

        return FakeConversationContext()


class FakeConversationService:
    """
    Security-focused conversation-service double.

    State is explicitly scoped by Telegram identity so
    accidental cross-user mixing becomes observable.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.calls: list[dict] = []
        self.sessions: dict[int, list[str]] = {}

    async def handle_telegram_message(
        self,
        *,
        telegram_user_id: int,
        message: str,
    ) -> str:
        self.calls.append(
            {
                "telegram_user_id": telegram_user_id,
                "message": message,
            }
        )

        history = self.sessions.setdefault(
            telegram_user_id,
            [],
        )

        history.append(message)

        return (
            f"response:{telegram_user_id}:"
            f"{len(history)}"
        )

    async def get_recent_history(
        self,
        *,
        telegram_user_id: int,
        limit: int = 20,
    ) -> list[str]:
        history = self.sessions.get(
            telegram_user_id,
            [],
        )

        return history[-limit:]


def make_boundary(
    *,
    approved_users: set[int] | None = None,
):
    access = FakeBetaAccessService(
        approved_users=approved_users,
    )

    conversation_service = FakeConversationService()

    boundary = BetaTelegramConversationBoundary(
        conversation_service=conversation_service,
        beta_access_service=access,
    )

    return (
        boundary,
        access,
        conversation_service,
    )

    )

    assert 999 not in conversation_service.sessions

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

import pytest

from app.application.beta_access.beta_telegram_conversation_boundary import (
    BetaTelegramConversationBoundary,
)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FakeConversationContext:
    world_id: str = "world-fr"
    character: str = "Alix"
    level: str = "B1"


class FakeBetaAccessService:
    """Deterministic Beta authorization/context test double."""

    def __init__(self, *, approved: bool = True) -> None:
        self.approved = approved
        self.calls: list[int] = []

    async def get_conversation_context(
        self,
        telegram_user_id: int,
    ) -> FakeConversationContext:
        self.calls.append(telegram_user_id)

        if not self.approved:
            raise PermissionError(
                "Telegram user is not approved."
            )

        return FakeConversationContext()


class FakeConversationService:
    """Deterministic downstream conversation-service double."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.calls: list[dict] = []

    async def handle_telegram_message(
        self,
        *,
        telegram_user_id: int,
        message: str,
    ) -> str:
        self.calls.append(
            {
                "telegram_user_id": telegram_user_id,
                "message": message,
            }
        )
        return "Bonjour !"


class FakeRateLimiter:
    """
    Deterministic WS-11 rate-limit policy double.

    The limiter is intentionally placed at the application boundary
    in these integration tests. Production wiring may provide a
    different implementation.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        limit: int = 3,
    ) -> None:
        self.limit = limit
        self.calls: list[int] = []
        self._counts: dict[int, int] = {}

    async def allow(
        self,
        *,
        telegram_user_id: int,
    ) -> bool:
        self.calls.append(telegram_user_id)

        count = self._counts.get(
            telegram_user_id,
            0,
        )

        if count >= self.limit:
            return False

        self._counts[telegram_user_id] = count + 1
        return True


class RateLimitedBoundary:
    """
    Minimal WS-11 integration composition.

    This test composition intentionally keeps rate limiting separate
    from the conversation service and from Telegram transport.
    """

    RATE_LIMIT_RESPONSE = (
        "You have reached the classroom message limit. "
        "Please try again later."
    )

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        conversation_service: FakeConversationService,
        beta_access_service: FakeBetaAccessService,
        rate_limiter: FakeRateLimiter,
    ) -> None:
        self._conversation_service = conversation_service
        self._beta_access_service = beta_access_service
        self._rate_limiter = rate_limiter

        self._conversation_boundary = BetaTelegramConversationBoundary(
            conversation_service=conversation_service,
            beta_access_service=beta_access_service,
        )

    async def handle_message(
        self,
        *,
        telegram_user_id: int,
        message: str,
    ) -> str:
        # Input validation remains owned by the existing boundary.
        # Rate limiting is applied before downstream conversation
        # processing.
        if not await self._rate_limiter.allow(
            telegram_user_id=telegram_user_id,
        ):
            return self.RATE_LIMIT_RESPONSE

        return await self._conversation_boundary.handle_message(
            telegram_user_id=telegram_user_id,
            message=message,
        )


def make_boundary(
    *,
    approved: bool = True,
    limit: int = 3,
):
    access = FakeBetaAccessService(
        approved=approved,
    )
    conversation_service = FakeConversationService()
    rate_limiter = FakeRateLimiter(
        limit=limit,
    )

    boundary = RateLimitedBoundary(
        conversation_service=conversation_service,
        beta_access_service=access,
        rate_limiter=rate_limiter,
    )

    return (
        boundary,
        access,
        conversation_service,
        rate_limiter,
    )


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_ws11_messages_within_limit_reach_conversation_service():
    (
        boundary,
        access,
        conversation_service,
        rate_limiter,
    ) = make_boundary(limit=3)

    for message in (
        "Bonjour",
        "Comment allez-vous ?",
        "Merci !",
    ):
        response = await boundary.handle_message(
            telegram_user_id=12345,
            message=message,
        )

        assert response == "Bonjour !"

    assert rate_limiter.calls == [
        12345,
        12345,
        12345,
    ]

    assert access.calls == [
        12345,
        12345,
        12345,
    ]

    assert conversation_service.calls == [
        {
            "telegram_user_id": 12345,
            "message": "Bonjour",
        },
        {
            "telegram_user_id": 12345,
            "message": "Comment allez-vous ?",
        },
        {
            "telegram_user_id": 12345,
            "message": "Merci !",
        },
    ]

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

import pytest

from app.application.beta_access.beta_telegram_conversation_boundary import (
    BetaTelegramConversationBoundary,
)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FakeConversationContext:
    world_id: str = "world-fr"
    character: str = "Alix"
    level: str = "B1"


class FakeBetaAccessService:
    """Deterministic Beta authorization/context test double."""

    def __init__(self, *, approved: bool = True) -> None:
        self.approved = approved
        self.calls: list[int] = []

    async def get_conversation_context(
        self,
        telegram_user_id: int,
    ) -> FakeConversationContext:
        self.calls.append(telegram_user_id)

        if not self.approved:
            raise PermissionError(
                "Telegram user is not approved."
            )

        return FakeConversationContext()


class FakeConversationService:
    """Deterministic downstream conversation-service double."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.calls: list[dict] = []

    async def handle_telegram_message(
        self,
        *,
        telegram_user_id: int,
        message: str,
    ) -> str:
        self.calls.append(
            {
                "telegram_user_id": telegram_user_id,
                "message": message,
            }
        )
        return "Bonjour !"


class FakeAbuseProtector:
    """
    Deterministic WS-12 abuse-protection policy double.

    The policy counts accepted requests per Telegram identity and
    blocks requests after the configured burst threshold.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        max_messages: int = 3,
    ) -> None:
        self.max_messages = max_messages
        self.calls: list[int] = []
        self._counts: dict[int, int] = {}

    async def allow(
        self,
        *,
        telegram_user_id: int,
    ) -> bool:
        self.calls.append(telegram_user_id)

        count = self._counts.get(
            telegram_user_id,
            0,
        )

        if count >= self.max_messages:
            return False

        self._counts[telegram_user_id] = count + 1
        return True


class AbuseProtectedBoundary:
    """
    Minimal WS-12 integration composition.

    Abuse protection remains a separate application policy and does
    not belong inside the Telegram transport adapter or conversation
    service.
    """

    ABUSE_LIMIT_RESPONSE = (
        "Sorry, you are sending messages too quickly. "
        "Please wait a moment and try again."
    )

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        conversation_service: FakeConversationService,
        beta_access_service: FakeBetaAccessService,
        abuse_protector: FakeAbuseProtector,
    ) -> None:
        self._conversation_service = conversation_service
        self._beta_access_service = beta_access_service
        self._abuse_protector = abuse_protector

        self._conversation_boundary = BetaTelegramConversationBoundary(
            conversation_service=conversation_service,
            beta_access_service=beta_access_service,
        )

    async def handle_message(
        self,
        *,
        telegram_user_id: int,
        message: str,
    ) -> str:
        # Input validation remains owned by the established
        # conversation boundary.
        self._conversation_boundary._validate_telegram_user_id(
            telegram_user_id,
        )
        self._conversation_boundary._validate_message(
            message,
        )

        if not await self._abuse_protector.allow(
            telegram_user_id=telegram_user_id,
        ):
            return self.ABUSE_LIMIT_RESPONSE

        return await self._conversation_boundary.handle_message(
            telegram_user_id=telegram_user_id,
            message=message,
        )


def make_boundary(
    *,
    approved: bool = True,
    max_messages: int = 3,
):
    access = FakeBetaAccessService(
        approved=approved,
    )
    conversation_service = FakeConversationService()
    abuse_protector = FakeAbuseProtector(
        max_messages=max_messages,
    )

    boundary = AbuseProtectedBoundary(
        conversation_service=conversation_service,
        beta_access_service=access,
        abuse_protector=abuse_protector,
    )

    return (
        boundary,
        access,
        conversation_service,
        abuse_protector,
    )

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

import pytest

from app.application.beta_access.beta_telegram_conversation_boundary import (
    BetaTelegramConversationBoundary,
)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FakeConversationContext:
    world_id: str = "world-fr"
    character: str = "Alix"
    level: str = "B1"


class FakeBetaAccessService:
    """Deterministic Beta authorization/context test double."""

    def __init__(self, *, approved: bool = True) -> None:
        self.approved = approved
        self.calls: list[int] = []

    async def get_conversation_context(
        self,
        telegram_user_id: int,
    ) -> FakeConversationContext:
        self.calls.append(telegram_user_id)

        if not self.approved:
            raise PermissionError(
                "Telegram user is not approved."
            )

        return FakeConversationContext()


class FakeConversationService:
    """Deterministic conversation-service test double."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        response: str = "Bonjour !",
        error: Exception | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.response = response
        self.error = error
        self.calls: list[dict] = []

    async def handle_telegram_message(
        self,
        *,
        telegram_user_id: int,
        message: str,
    ) -> str:
        self.calls.append(
            {
                "telegram_user_id": telegram_user_id,
                "message": message,
            }
        )

        if self.error is not None:
            raise self.error

        return self.response


class FakeObservability:
    """
    Deterministic WS-13 observability/audit event sink.

    Events intentionally contain only operational metadata. Raw
    learner message content is not accepted by the event contract.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        error: Exception | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.error = error
        self.events: list[dict] = []

    async def record(
        self,
        *,
        event_type: str,
        telegram_user_id: int,
        outcome: str,
    ) -> None:
        if self.error is not None:
            raise self.error

        self.events.append(
            {
                "event_type": event_type,
                "telegram_user_id": telegram_user_id,
                "outcome": outcome,
            }
        )


class ObservableBoundary:
    """
    Minimal WS-13 integration composition.

    Observability is deliberately separated from the conversation
    service. An observability failure must not become a classroom
    application failure.
    """

    SAFE_ERROR_RESPONSE = (
        "Sorry, something went wrong while processing your message. "
        "Please try again later."
    )

    UNAUTHORIZED_RESPONSE = (
        "Sorry, this Telegram account is not authorized "
        "for Beta access."
    )

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        conversation_service: FakeConversationService,
        beta_access_service: FakeBetaAccessService,
        observability: FakeObservability,
    ) -> None:
        self._conversation_service = conversation_service
        self._beta_access_service = beta_access_service
        self._observability = observability

    async def _record(
        self,
        *,
        event_type: str,
        telegram_user_id: int,
        outcome: str,
    ) -> None:
        try:
            await self._observability.record(
                event_type=event_type,
                telegram_user_id=telegram_user_id,
                outcome=outcome,
            )
        except Exception:
            # Observability is non-blocking infrastructure. Failure
            # must never break the classroom flow.
            return

    async def handle_message(
        self,
        *,
        telegram_user_id: int,
        message: str,
    ) -> str:
        if isinstance(telegram_user_id, bool):
            raise ValueError(
                "Telegram user ID must be a positive integer."
            )

        if not isinstance(telegram_user_id, int):
            raise TypeError(
                "Telegram user ID must be a positive integer."
            )

        if telegram_user_id <= 0:
            raise ValueError(
                "Telegram user ID must be a positive integer."
            )

        if message is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "Telegram message cannot be empty."
            )

        if not isinstance(message, str):
            raise TypeError(
                "Telegram message must be a string."
            )

        if not message.strip():
            raise ValueError(
                "Telegram message cannot be empty."
            )

        clean_message = message.strip()

        if len(clean_message) > 4096:
            raise ValueError(
                "Telegram message is too long. "
                "Maximum length is 4096 characters."
            )

        try:
            context = await (
                self._beta_access_service
                .get_conversation_context(
                    telegram_user_id
                )
            )
        except PermissionError:
            await self._record(
                event_type="telegram_classroom_authorization",
                telegram_user_id=telegram_user_id,
                outcome="denied",
            )

            return self.UNAUTHORIZED_RESPONSE

        # Context is operational metadata and is never injected into
        # the learner message or observability event content.
        _ = context

        try:
            response = await (
                self._conversation_service
                .handle_telegram_message(
                    telegram_user_id=telegram_user_id,
                    message=clean_message,
                )
            )
        except Exception:
            await self._record(
                event_type="telegram_classroom_conversation",
                telegram_user_id=telegram_user_id,
                outcome="error",
            )

            return self.SAFE_ERROR_RESPONSE

        await self._record(
            event_type="telegram_classroom_conversation",
            telegram_user_id=telegram_user_id,
            outcome="success",
        )

        return response


def make_boundary(
    *,
    approved: bool = True,
    conversation_error: Exception | None = None,
    observability_error: Exception | None = None,
):
    access = FakeBetaAccessService(
        approved=approved,
    )

    conversation_service = FakeConversationService(

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

import pytest

from app.application.beta_access.beta_telegram_conversation_boundary import (
    BetaTelegramConversationBoundary,
)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FakeConversationContext:
    world_id: str = "world-fr"
    character: str = "Alix"
    level: str = "B1"


class FakeBetaAccessService:
    """Deterministic Beta authorization/context test double."""

    def __init__(self, *, approved: bool = True) -> None:
        self.approved = approved
        self.calls: list[int] = []

    async def get_conversation_context(
        self,
        telegram_user_id: int,
    ) -> FakeConversationContext:
        self.calls.append(telegram_user_id)

        if not self.approved:
            raise PermissionError(
                "Telegram user is not approved."
            )

        return FakeConversationContext()


class FakeConversationService:
    """Deterministic downstream conversation-service double."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.calls: list[dict] = []

    async def handle_telegram_message(
        self,
        *,
        telegram_user_id: int,
        message: str,
    ) -> str:
        self.calls.append(
            {
                "telegram_user_id": telegram_user_id,
                "message": message,
            }
        )
        return "Bonjour !"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TelegramClassroomPolicy:
    """Configuration-driven WS-14 classroom policy."""

    max_message_length: int = 4096
    max_messages_per_user: int = 3
    enabled: bool = True


class TelegramClassroomPolicyValidator:
    """Validates classroom policy before it is used."""

    @staticmethod
    def validate(
        policy: TelegramClassroomPolicy,
    ) -> None:
        if not isinstance(policy, TelegramClassroomPolicy):
            raise TypeError(
                "Telegram classroom policy must be a "
                "TelegramClassroomPolicy."
            )

        if not isinstance(policy.max_message_length, int):
            raise TypeError(
                "max_message_length must be an integer."
            )

        if policy.max_message_length <= 0:
            raise ValueError(
                "max_message_length must be greater than zero."
            )

        if not isinstance(policy.max_messages_per_user, int):
            raise TypeError(
                "max_messages_per_user must be an integer."
            )

        if policy.max_messages_per_user <= 0:
            raise ValueError(
                "max_messages_per_user must be greater than zero."
            )

        if not isinstance(policy.enabled, bool):
            raise TypeError(
                "enabled must be a boolean."
            )


class FakePolicyEnforcer:
    """
    Deterministic policy enforcer.

    State is explicitly scoped by Telegram identity.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        policy: TelegramClassroomPolicy,
    ) -> None:
        TelegramClassroomPolicyValidator.validate(policy)

        self.policy = policy
        self.calls: list[int] = []
        self._counts: dict[int, int] = {}

    async def allow(
        self,
        *,
        telegram_user_id: int,
    ) -> bool:
        self.calls.append(telegram_user_id)

        if not self.policy.enabled:
            return False

        count = self._counts.get(
            telegram_user_id,
            0,
        )

        if count >= self.policy.max_messages_per_user:
            return False

        self._counts[telegram_user_id] = count + 1
        return True


class PolicyControlledBoundary:
    """
    Minimal WS-14 integration composition.

    Policy validation and enforcement are deliberately kept outside
    the Telegram transport adapter and conversation service.
    """

    POLICY_DISABLED_RESPONSE = (
        "Sorry, the classroom is temporarily unavailable."
    )

    POLICY_LIMIT_RESPONSE = (
        "Sorry, you have reached the classroom message limit. "
        "Please try again later."
    )

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        conversation_service: FakeConversationService,
        beta_access_service: FakeBetaAccessService,
        policy: TelegramClassroomPolicy,
    ) -> None:
        TelegramClassroomPolicyValidator.validate(policy)

        self.policy = policy
        self._conversation_service = conversation_service
        self._beta_access_service = beta_access_service
        self._policy_enforcer = FakePolicyEnforcer(
            policy=policy,
        )

        self._conversation_boundary = BetaTelegramConversationBoundary(
            conversation_service=conversation_service,
            beta_access_service=beta_access_service,
        )

    async def handle_message(
        self,
        *,
        telegram_user_id: int,
        message: str,
    ) -> str:
        # Reuse the established WS-10 input validation contract before
        # consuming any configured classroom allowance.
        BetaTelegramConversationBoundary._validate_telegram_user_id(
            telegram_user_id,
        )

        clean_message = (
            BetaTelegramConversationBoundary._validate_message(
                message,
            )
        )

        if not self.policy.enabled:
            return self.POLICY_DISABLED_RESPONSE

        if len(clean_message) > self.policy.max_message_length:
            raise ValueError(
                "Telegram message is too long for the configured "
                "classroom policy."
            )

        if not await self._policy_enforcer.allow(
            telegram_user_id=telegram_user_id,
        ):
            return self.POLICY_LIMIT_RESPONSE

        return await self._conversation_boundary.handle_message(
            telegram_user_id=telegram_user_id,
            message=clean_message,
        )


def make_boundary(
    *,
    approved: bool = True,
    policy: TelegramClassroomPolicy | None = None,
):
    if policy is None:
        policy = TelegramClassroomPolicy()

    access = FakeBetaAccessService(
        approved=approved,
    )
    conversation_service = FakeConversationService()

    boundary = PolicyControlledBoundary(
        conversation_service=conversation_service,
        beta_access_service=access,
        policy=policy,
    )

    return (
        boundary,
        access,
        conversation_service,
    )


def test_ws14_default_policy_is_valid():

    TelegramClassroomPolicyValidator.validate(policy)

    assert policy.enabled is True
    assert policy.max_message_length == 4096
    assert policy.max_messages_per_user == 3

)
def test_ws14_invalid_zero_or_negative_policy_is_rejected(

        TelegramClassroomPolicyValidator.validate(policy)


def test_ws14_invalid_policy_types_are_rejected():
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        TelegramClassroomPolicyValidator.validate(
            TelegramClassroomPolicy(
                max_message_length="4096",  # type: ignore[arg-type]
            )
        )

    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        TelegramClassroomPolicyValidator.validate(
            TelegramClassroomPolicy(
                max_messages_per_user="3",  # type: ignore[arg-type]
            )
        )

    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        TelegramClassroomPolicyValidator.validate(
            TelegramClassroomPolicy(
                enabled="yes",  # type: ignore[arg-type]
            )
        )

@dataclass(frozen=True)

    world_id: str = "world-fr"

    async def get_conversation_context(
        self,

        self.calls.append(telegram_user_id)

class FakeConversationService:
    def __init__(
        self,
        response: str = "Bonjour ! Continuons notre conversation.",
        error: Exception | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.response = response
        self.error = error
        self.calls: list[dict] = []

    async def handle_telegram_message(
        self,
        *,
        telegram_user_id: int,
        message: str,
    ) -> str:
        self.calls.append(
            {
                "telegram_user_id": telegram_user_id,
                "message": message,
            }
        )

        if self.error is not None:
            raise self.error

        return self.response


class FakeStartHandler:
    async def handle(self, **kwargs) -> None:
        await kwargs["reply"]("started")


def make_composition(
    *,
    gate_allowed: bool = True,
    beta_approved: bool = True,
    conversation_error: Exception | None = None,
):

from dataclasses import dataclass

import pytest

from app.infrastructure.telegram.telegram_bot_runtime import (

@dataclass
class FakeUser:
    id: int


@dataclass
class FakeChat:
    id: int
    type: str


class FakeMessage:
    def __init__(self, text: str | None) -> None:
        self.text = text
        self.replies: list[str] = []

    async def reply_text(self, text: str) -> None:
        self.replies.append(text)


@dataclass
class FakeUpdate:
    effective_user: FakeUser
    effective_chat: FakeChat
    effective_message: FakeMessage


class FakeContext:
    args: list[str] = []


class FakeGate:
    def __init__(self, allowed: bool = True) -> None:
        self.allowed = allowed
        self.calls: list[dict] = []

    async def authorize(
        self,
        *,
        telegram_user_id: int,
        chat_type: str,
    ) -> bool:
        self.calls.append(
            {
                "telegram_user_id": telegram_user_id,
                "chat_type": chat_type,
            }
        )
        return self.allowed


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FakeConversationContext:
    world_id: str = "world-fr"
    character: str = "Alix"
    level: str = "B1"


class FakeBetaAccessService:
    def __init__(self, approved: bool = True) -> None:
        self.approved = approved
        self.calls: list[int] = []

    async def get_conversation_context(
        self,
        telegram_user_id: int,
    ) -> FakeConversationContext:
        self.calls.append(telegram_user_id)

        if not self.approved:
            raise PermissionError(
                "Telegram user is not approved."
            )

        return FakeConversationContext()


class FakeConversationService:
    def __init__(
        self,
        response: str = "Bonjour !",
        error: Exception | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.response = response
        self.error = error
        self.calls: list[dict] = []

    async def handle_telegram_message(
        self,
        *,
        telegram_user_id: int,
        message: str,
    ) -> str:
        self.calls.append(
            {
                "telegram_user_id": telegram_user_id,
                "message": message,
            }
        )

        if self.error is not None:
            raise self.error

        return self.response


class FakeStartHandler:
    async def handle(self, **kwargs) -> None:
        await kwargs["reply"]("started")


def make_runtime(
    *,
    gate_allowed: bool = True,
    beta_approved: bool = True,
    conversation_error: Exception | None = None,
):
    from app.application.beta_access.beta_telegram_conversation_boundary import (
        BetaTelegramConversationBoundary,
    )

    gate = FakeGate(gate_allowed)
    access = FakeBetaAccessService(beta_approved)
    conversation_service = FakeConversationService(
        error=conversation_error,
    )

    boundary = BetaTelegramConversationBoundary(
        conversation_service=conversation_service,
        beta_access_service=access,
    )

    adapter = BetaTelegramAdapter(
        start_handler=FakeStartHandler(),
        private_chat_gate=gate,
        conversation_boundary=boundary,
    )

    runtime = TelegramBotRuntime(
        adapter=adapter,
        conversation_boundary=boundary,
    )

    return (
        runtime,
        adapter,
        gate,
        access,
        conversation_service,
    )

class FakeContext:

    character = "Alix"
    level = "B1"

class FakeConversation:
    """Minimal conversation service test double."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        response: str = "Bonjour !",
        error: Exception | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.calls: list[tuple[int, str, object]] = []
        self.response = response
        self.error = error

    async def handle_telegram_message_with_context(
        self,
        *,
        telegram_user_id: int,
        message: str,
        context,
    ):
        self.calls.append(
            (
                telegram_user_id,
                message,
                context,
            )
        )

        if self.error is not None:
            raise self.error

        return self.response

@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_rate_limit_message_uses_active_world_language():
    limiter = InMemoryTelegramRateLimiter(
        max_messages=1,
        window_seconds=60,
    )

    conversation = FakeConversation()

    boundary = BetaTelegramConversationBoundary(
        conversation_service=conversation,
        beta_access_service=FakeAccess(),
        rate_limiter=limiter,
    )

    await boundary.handle_message(
        telegram_user_id=555,
        message="Bonjour",
    )

    response = await boundary.handle_message(
        telegram_user_id=555,
        message="Encore",

    )

    assert (
        "Tu pourras reprendre ta pratique vers"
        in response
    )

    assert ":" in response

    assert len(conversation.calls) == 1

        max_messages=1,
        window_seconds=60,
    )

        max_messages=1,
        window_seconds=60,
    )

    conversation = FakeConversation()

        conversation_service=conversation,
        beta_access_service=FakeAccess(),
        rate_limiter=limiter,
        abuse_protector=abuse,
    )

    with pytest.raises(
        ValueError,
        match="cannot be empty",

        await boundary.handle_message(
            telegram_user_id=1,
            message="   ",
        )

    assert await limiter.allow(
        telegram_user_id=1,
    )

    assert await abuse.allow(
        telegram_user_id=1,
    )
