# WS-19.13 â€” Observability
# ============================================================================


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_ws19_observability_does_not_log_raw_identity_or_content(
    caplog,
):
    """
    AC13 + AC15:
        Operational telemetry must not expose raw Telegram identity or
        learner message content.
    """

    composition = _build_composition()

    try:
        observability = (
            composition.conversation_boundary
            ._observability
        )

        telegram_user_id = (
            950000
            + int(uuid4().int % 10000)
        )

        learner_content = (
            f"WS19-secret-{uuid4().hex}"
        )

        caplog.set_level(
            logging.INFO,
        )

        await observability.record(
            event_type=(
                "telegram_classroom_message"
            ),
            telegram_user_id=telegram_user_id,
            outcome="accepted",
            metadata={
                "world_id": "world-fr",
                "character": "Alix",
                "level": "B1",
            },
        )

        log_text = "\n".join(
            record.getMessage()
            for record in caplog.records
        )

        assert (
            str(telegram_user_id)
            not in log_text
        )

        assert learner_content not in log_text

    finally:
        _dispose_composition(composition)


# ============================================================================
# WS-19.14 â€” Safe runtime failure
# ============================================================================


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_ws19_runtime_failure_returns_safe_response():
    """
    AC14:
        A runtime failure produces the safe learner-facing response.

    The authorization seam is replaced only for this test so that the
    message can reach the runtime failure path.
    """

    composition = _build_composition()

    try:
        boundary = (
            composition.conversation_boundary
        )

        service = (
            composition.conversation_service
        )

        class FakeApprovedContext:
            world_id = "world-fr"
            name = "French World"
            language_code = "fr"
            character = "Alix"
            level = "B1"

        async def approved_context(
            telegram_user_id: int,
        ):
            return FakeApprovedContext()

        monkeypatch = pytest.MonkeyPatch()

        try:
            monkeypatch.setattr(
                composition.beta_access_service,
                "get_conversation_context",
                approved_context,
            )

            runtime_attribute = None

            for name in (
                "_runtime",
                "_conversation_runtime",
            ):
                if hasattr(service, name):
                    runtime_attribute = name
                    break

            if runtime_attribute is None:
                pytest.skip(
                    "Conversation service does not expose "
                    "a replaceable runtime seam."
                )

            class FailingRuntime:
                async def respond(
                    self,
                    **kwargs,
                ):
                    raise RuntimeError(
                        "database password=WS19-secret"
                    )

            monkeypatch.setattr(
                service,
                runtime_attribute,
                FailingRuntime(),
            )

            response = await boundary.handle_message(
                telegram_user_id=960001,
                message="Bonjour",
            )

            assert (
                response
                == boundary.SAFE_ERROR_RESPONSE
            )

            assert "WS19-secret" not in response
            assert "password" not in response.lower()

        finally:
            monkeypatch.undo()

    finally:
        _dispose_composition(composition)

from __future__ import annotations

from unittest.mock import AsyncMock

import pytest
from fastapi import FastAPI
from httpx import ASGITransport, AsyncClient

from app.api.authentication import router as authentication_router
from app.application.identity.authentication_service import AuthenticationError


pytestmark = pytest.mark.integration


def _create_app(
    authentication_service: AsyncMock,
) -> FastAPI:
    app = FastAPI()
    app.state.authentication_service = authentication_service
    app.include_router(authentication_router)
    return app


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_password_reset_request_returns_generic_accepted_response() -> None:
    service = AsyncMock()

    app = _create_app(service)

    async with AsyncClient(
        transport=ASGITransport(app=app),
        base_url="http://test",
    ) as client:
        response = await client.post(
            "/auth/password-reset/request",
            json={"email": "user@example.com"},
        )

    assert response.status_code == 202

    assert response.json() == {
        "detail": (
            "If an account exists for that email address, "
            "a password reset email has been sent."
        )
    }

    service.request_password_reset.assert_awaited_once_with(
        email="user@example.com",
    )


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_password_reset_request_does_not_disclose_unknown_email() -> None:
    service = AsyncMock()

    service.request_password_reset.return_value = None

    app = _create_app(service)

    async with AsyncClient(
        transport=ASGITransport(app=app),
        base_url="http://test",
    ) as client:
        response = await client.post(
            "/auth/password-reset/request",
            json={"email": "unknown@example.com"},
        )

    assert response.status_code == 202

    assert "unknown@example.com" not in response.text
    assert "does not exist" not in response.text.lower()
    assert "not found" not in response.text.lower()


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_password_reset_request_maps_authentication_error_to_bad_request() -> None:
    service = AsyncMock()

    service.request_password_reset.side_effect = AuthenticationError(
        "A valid email is required."
    )

    app = _create_app(service)

    async with AsyncClient(
        transport=ASGITransport(app=app),
        base_url="http://test",
    ) as client:
        response = await client.post(
            "/auth/password-reset/request",
            json={"email": "invalid@example.com"},
        )

    assert response.status_code == 400
    assert response.json()["detail"] == "A valid email is required."

from __future__ import annotations

from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, MagicMock, patch

import pytest

from app.api.authentication import router as authentication_router
from app.main import create_application, lifespan


def test_authentication_router_defines_required_endpoints() -> None:
    """The canonical authentication router exposes all required endpoints."""

    route_paths = {
        route.path
        for route in authentication_router.routes
        if hasattr(route, "path")
    }

    assert route_paths == {
        "/auth/register",
        "/auth/login",
        "/auth/password-reset/request",
        "/auth/password-reset/confirm",
        "/auth/password-reset/context",
        "/auth/verify-email",
        "/auth/logout",
        "/auth/session",
    }


def test_create_application_composes_authentication_repository() -> None:
    """Application composition creates the auth repository from the canonical session factory."""

    fake_engine = MagicMock(name="auth_engine")
    fake_session_factory = MagicMock(name="auth_session_factory")

    with (
        patch(
            "app.main.create_async_database_engine",
            return_value=fake_engine,
        ),
        patch(
            "app.main.create_async_session_factory",
            return_value=fake_session_factory,
        ),
        patch(
            "app.main.PostgreSQLAuthenticationRepository",
        ) as repository_factory,
        patch(
            "app.main.create_cybersecurity_scheduler_runtime",
            return_value=MagicMock(),
        ),
    ):
        application = create_application()

    repository_factory.assert_called_once_with(
        fake_session_factory,
    )

    assert application.state.auth_engine is fake_engine
    assert application.state.auth_repository is (
        repository_factory.return_value
    )


def test_create_application_composes_authentication_router() -> None:
    """Application composition explicitly registers the canonical auth router."""

    fake_engine = MagicMock(name="auth_engine")
    fake_session_factory = MagicMock(name="auth_session_factory")

    with (
        patch(
            "app.main.create_async_database_engine",
            return_value=fake_engine,
        ),
        patch(
            "app.main.create_async_session_factory",
            return_value=fake_session_factory,
        ),
        patch(
            "app.main.PostgreSQLAuthenticationRepository",
        ),
        patch(
            "app.main.create_cybersecurity_scheduler_runtime",
            return_value=MagicMock(),
        ),
        patch(
            "app.main.FastAPI.include_router",
        ) as include_router,
    ):
        create_application()

    registered_routers = [
        call.args[0]
        for call in include_router.call_args_list
        if call.args
    ]

    assert authentication_router in registered_routers

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import FrozenInstanceError
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

import pytest

from app.application.identity.authentication_assurance import (
    AuthenticationAssuranceService,
    StaticAuthenticationAssurancePolicy,
)
from app.domain.identity.authentication_assurance import (
    AuthenticationAssuranceDecision,
    AuthenticationAssuranceFailure,
    AuthenticationAssuranceLevel,
    ValidatedAuthenticationEvidence,
)


class FixedClock:
    def __init__(self, current_time: datetime) -> None:
        self.current_time = current_time
        self.calls = 0

    def now(self) -> datetime:
        self.calls += 1
        return self.current_time


def make_evidence(
    *,
    principal_id: str = "user-123",
    audience: str = "easychatbot",
    authentication_time: datetime | None = None,
    authentication_method: str = "password",
    authentication_strength: str = "normal",
    user_verified: bool = False,
    phishing_resistant: bool = False,
) -> ValidatedAuthenticationEvidence:
    if authentication_time is None:
        authentication_time = datetime(
            2026,
            9,
            13,
            12,
            0,
            tzinfo=timezone.utc,
        )

    return ValidatedAuthenticationEvidence(
        principal_id=principal_id,
        issuer="trusted-test-issuer",
        subject="subject-123",
        audience=audience,
        authentication_time=authentication_time,
        authentication_method=authentication_method,
        authentication_strength=authentication_strength,
        user_verified=user_verified,
        phishing_resistant=phishing_resistant,
        evidence_id="evidence-123",
        policy_version="test-policy-v1",
    )


def make_service(
    *,
    now: datetime | None = None,
    policy: StaticAuthenticationAssurancePolicy | None = None,
) -> tuple[AuthenticationAssuranceService, FixedClock]:
    if now is None:
        now = datetime(
            2026,
            9,
            13,
            12,
            1,
            tzinfo=timezone.utc,
        )

    clock = FixedClock(now)

    if policy is None:
        policy = StaticAuthenticationAssurancePolicy()

    service = AuthenticationAssuranceService(
        policy=policy,
        clock=clock,
    )

    return service, clock


def test_assurance_ordering_is_monotonic() -> None:
    assert (
        AuthenticationAssuranceLevel.A0
        < AuthenticationAssuranceLevel.A1
        < AuthenticationAssuranceLevel.A2
        < AuthenticationAssuranceLevel.A3
    )


def test_a3_cannot_be_caller_forged_by_setting_an_assurance_level() -> None:
    evidence = make_evidence()

    assert not hasattr(evidence, "assurance_level")

    service, _ = make_service()

    result = service.require(
        principal_id="user-123",
        required_level=AuthenticationAssuranceLevel.A3,
        expected_audience="easychatbot",
        evidence=evidence,
    )

    assert result.decision is AuthenticationAssuranceDecision.DENY
    assert (
        result.failure
        is AuthenticationAssuranceFailure.INSUFFICIENT_AUTHENTICATION_ASSURANCE
    )


def test_a3_requires_phishing_resistant_user_verified_evidence() -> None:

        authentication_strength="strong",
        user_verified=True,
        phishing_resistant=True,
    )

    service, _ = make_service()

    result = service.require(

        required_level=AuthenticationAssuranceLevel.A3,
        expected_audience="easychatbot",
        evidence=evidence,
    )

    assert result.decision is AuthenticationAssuranceDecision.ALLOW
    assert result.failure is None
    assert result.context is not None
    assert result.context.assurance_level is AuthenticationAssuranceLevel.A3


def test_trusted_clock_is_used_for_freshness() -> None:
    trusted_now = datetime(
        2026,
        9,
        13,
        12,
        10,

    )

    assert result.context is not None

        user_id="operator-1",
        email="operator@example.com",
        email_verified=True,
        account_status=AccountStatus.ACTIVE,
        roles=frozenset({"operator"}),
    )

        user_id="admin-1",
        email="admin@example.com",
        email_verified=True,
        account_status=AccountStatus.ACTIVE,
        roles=frozenset({"admin"}),
    )

    return Principal(
        user_id="beta-1",
        email="beta@example.com",
        email_verified=True,
        account_status=AccountStatus.ACTIVE,
        roles=frozenset({"beta_user"}),
    )


def test_operator_can_publish_announcements():
    principal = AuthorizationService().require_permission(
        principal=operator(),
        permission=Permission.ANNOUNCEMENT_PUBLISH,
    )
    assert principal.user_id == "operator-1"


def test_beta_user_cannot_publish_announcements():
    try:
        AuthorizationService().require_permission(
            principal=beta_user(),
            permission=Permission.ANNOUNCEMENT_PUBLISH,
        )
    except PermissionDeniedError:
        return

    raise AssertionError("Beta users must not publish announcements.")

    principal = AuthorizationService().require_permission(
        principal=operator(),
        permission=Permission.FUNCTIONALITY_CONTROL,
    )
    assert principal.user_id == "operator-1"

        principal=admin(),
        permission=Permission.FUNCTIONALITY_CONTROL,
    )
    assert principal.user_id == "admin-1"


def test_beta_user_cannot_control_functionality():
    try:
        AuthorizationService().require_permission(
            principal=beta_user(),
            permission=Permission.FUNCTIONALITY_CONTROL,
        )
    except PermissionDeniedError:
        return

    raise AssertionError("Beta users must not control functionalities.")

from __future__ import annotations

from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from dataclasses import FrozenInstanceError
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

import pytest

from app.domain.identity.authentication_assurance import (
    AuthenticationAssuranceContext,
    AuthenticationAssuranceLevel,
)

from app.domain.identity.transaction_authorization import (
    AuthorizationIdRegistry,
    CanonicalTransaction,
    NonceRegistry,
    TransactionAuthorization,
    TransactionAuthorizationConsumer,
    TransactionAuthorizationDecision,
    TransactionAuthorizationFailure,
    TransactionAuthorizationRegistry,
    TransactionAuthorizationState,
    TrustedApprovalEvidence,
    attach_approval,
    consume,
    expire_if_due,
    transition,
)


class FixedClock:
    def __init__(self, value: datetime) -> None:
        self.value = value

    def now(self) -> datetime:
        return self.value


@pytest.fixture
def now() -> datetime:
    return datetime(2026, 9, 13, 20, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)


@pytest.fixture
def clock(now: datetime) -> FixedClock:
    return FixedClock(now)


@pytest.fixture
def transaction(now: datetime) -> CanonicalTransaction:
    return CanonicalTransaction.from_mapping(
        transaction_id="tx-001",
        principal_id="user-001",
        amount="100.00",
        currency="eur",
        merchant_or_service="merchant.example",
        operation="purchase",
        timestamp=now,
        nonce="nonce-001",
        risk_context={"risk": "medium", "channel": "web"},
    )


@pytest.fixture
def authorization(
    transaction: CanonicalTransaction,
    now: datetime,
) -> TransactionAuthorization:
    return TransactionAuthorization(
        authorization_id="auth-001",
        transaction=transaction,
        created_at=now,
        expires_at=now + timedelta(minutes=5),
    )


def assurance_context(
    *,
    principal_id: str = "user-001",
    level: AuthenticationAssuranceLevel = AuthenticationAssuranceLevel.A2,
    assurance_time: datetime | None = None,
) -> AuthenticationAssuranceContext:
    assurance_time = assurance_time or datetime(
        2026,
        9,
        13,
        19,
        59,
        tzinfo=timezone.utc,
    )

    return AuthenticationAssuranceContext(
        principal_id=principal_id,
        assurance_level=level,
        authentication_time=assurance_time,
        assurance_time=assurance_time,
        authentication_method="password",
        authentication_strength="mfa",
        user_verified=True,
        phishing_resistant=level is AuthenticationAssuranceLevel.A3,
        issuer="easychatbot-test",
        subject=principal_id,
        audience="easychatbot",
        evidence_id="assurance-evidence-001",
        policy_version="W15.6-policy-v1",
    )


def approved_authorization(
    authorization: TransactionAuthorization,
    clock: FixedClock,
    *,
    level: AuthenticationAssuranceLevel = AuthenticationAssuranceLevel.A2,
    principal_id: str = "user-001",
) -> TransactionAuthorization:
    pending = transition(
        authorization,
        TransactionAuthorizationState.PENDING_USER_APPROVAL,
    )

    approval = TrustedApprovalEvidence(
        authorization_id=authorization.authorization_id,
        transaction=authorization.transaction,
        approved_at=clock.now(),
        evidence_id=f"approval-{authorization.authorization_id}",
        assurance_context=assurance_context(
            principal_id=principal_id,
            level=level,
            assurance_time=clock.now(),
        ),
    )

    return attach_approval(
        pending,
        approval,
        clock=clock,
    )


def test_assurance_ordering() -> None:
    assert AuthenticationAssuranceLevel.A0.value < AuthenticationAssuranceLevel.A1.value
    assert AuthenticationAssuranceLevel.A1.value < AuthenticationAssuranceLevel.A2.value
    assert AuthenticationAssuranceLevel.A2.value < AuthenticationAssuranceLevel.A3.value


def test_validated_assurance_is_immutable() -> None:
    value = assurance_context()

    with pytest.raises(FrozenInstanceError):
        value.assurance_level = AuthenticationAssuranceLevel.A3  # type: ignore[misc]


def test_assurance_requires_validated_enum_not_arbitrary_integer(
    transaction: CanonicalTransaction,
    now: datetime,
) -> None:
    context = assurance_context(
        principal_id=transaction.principal_id,
        level=AuthenticationAssuranceLevel.A2,
        assurance_time=now,
    )

    # Simulate malformed runtime data crossing the W15.6 -> W15.7
    # trust boundary. W15.6's frozen dataclass is the authoritative type;
    # this does not create a second assurance authority.
    object.__setattr__(context, "assurance_level", 999)

    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="AuthenticationAssuranceLevel"):
        TrustedApprovalEvidence(
            authorization_id="auth-malformed-assurance",
            transaction=transaction,
            approved_at=now,
            evidence_id="malformed-assurance",
            assurance_context=context,
        )

def test_every_security_field_changes_canonical_binding(
    transaction: CanonicalTransaction,
) -> None:
    values = {
        "transaction_id": "tx-changed",
        "principal_id": "user-changed",
        "operation": "refund",
        "amount": "101.00",
        "currency": "USD",
        "merchant_or_service": "other.example",
        "timestamp": transaction.timestamp + timedelta(seconds=1),
        "nonce": "nonce-changed",
        "risk_context": {"risk": "high", "channel": "web"},
    }

    for field, value in values.items():
        kwargs = {
            "transaction_id": transaction.transaction_id,
            "principal_id": transaction.principal_id,
            "amount": transaction.amount,
            "currency": transaction.currency,
            "merchant_or_service": transaction.merchant_or_service,
            "operation": transaction.operation,
            "timestamp": transaction.timestamp,
            "nonce": transaction.nonce,
            "risk_context": dict(transaction.risk_context),
        }

        kwargs[field] = value

        changed = CanonicalTransaction.from_mapping(**kwargs)

        assert (
            changed.canonical_representation()
            != transaction.canonical_representation()
        ), field


def test_transaction_binding_covers_required_security_fields(
    transaction: CanonicalTransaction,
) -> None:
    representation = transaction.canonical_representation()

    for value in (
        transaction.transaction_id,
        transaction.principal_id,
        transaction.operation,
        transaction.nonce,
        transaction.currency,
        transaction.merchant_or_service,
        "medium",
        "web",
        "100.00",
    ):
        assert value in representation

def test_legal_lifecycle_transitions(
    authorization: TransactionAuthorization,
    clock: FixedClock,
) -> None:
    pending = transition(
        authorization,
        TransactionAuthorizationState.PENDING_USER_APPROVAL,
    )

    approved = approved_authorization(
        authorization,
        clock,
    )

    consumed = transition(
        approved,
        TransactionAuthorizationState.CONSUMED,
    )

    assert pending.state is TransactionAuthorizationState.PENDING_USER_APPROVAL
    assert approved.state is TransactionAuthorizationState.APPROVED
    assert consumed.state is TransactionAuthorizationState.CONSUMED


def test_illegal_lifecycle_transitions_fail_closed(
    authorization: TransactionAuthorization,
) -> None:
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        transition(
            authorization,
            TransactionAuthorizationState.CONSUMED,
        )

    pending = transition(
        authorization,
        TransactionAuthorizationState.PENDING_USER_APPROVAL,
    )

    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        transition(
            pending,
            TransactionAuthorizationState.CONSUMED,
        )

def test_registry_replace_requires_expected_current_state(
    authorization: TransactionAuthorization,
) -> None:
    registry = TransactionAuthorizationRegistry()

    registry.register(authorization)

    replacement = transition(
        authorization,
        TransactionAuthorizationState.PENDING_USER_APPROVAL,
    )

    wrong_expected = transition(
        authorization,
        TransactionAuthorizationState.PENDING_USER_APPROVAL,
    )

    assert not registry.replace(
        authorization.authorization_id,
        wrong_expected,
        replacement,
    )

    assert registry.replace(
        authorization.authorization_id,
        authorization,
        replacement,
    )


def test_atomic_consume_is_single_use(
    authorization: TransactionAuthorization,
    clock: FixedClock,
) -> None:
    approved = approved_authorization(
        authorization,
        clock,
    )

    registry = TransactionAuthorizationRegistry()
    registry.register(approved)

    consumer = TransactionAuthorizationConsumer(registry)

    first = consumer.consume_once(
        authorization.authorization_id,
        expected_transaction=authorization.transaction,
        clock=clock,
        required_assurance_level=AuthenticationAssuranceLevel.A2,
    )

    second = consumer.consume_once(
        authorization.authorization_id,
        expected_transaction=authorization.transaction,
        clock=clock,
        required_assurance_level=AuthenticationAssuranceLevel.A2,
    )

    assert first.decision is TransactionAuthorizationDecision.ALLOW
    assert second.decision is TransactionAuthorizationDecision.DENY
    assert second.failure is TransactionAuthorizationFailure.ALREADY_CONSUMED


def test_concurrent_consumption_has_exactly_one_success(
    authorization: TransactionAuthorization,
    clock: FixedClock,
) -> None:
    approved = approved_authorization(
        authorization,
        clock,
    )

    registry = TransactionAuthorizationRegistry()
    registry.register(approved)

    consumer = TransactionAuthorizationConsumer(registry)

    def attempt():
        return consumer.consume_once(
            authorization.authorization_id,
            expected_transaction=authorization.transaction,
            clock=clock,
            required_assurance_level=AuthenticationAssuranceLevel.A2,
        )

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=16) as executor:
        results = list(
            executor.map(
                lambda _: attempt(),
                range(16),
            )
        )

    allows = [
        result
        for result in results
        if result.decision is TransactionAuthorizationDecision.ALLOW
    ]

    assert len(allows) == 1


def test_transaction_mismatch_denies(
    authorization: TransactionAuthorization,
    clock: FixedClock,
) -> None:
    approved = approved_authorization(
        authorization,
        clock,
    )

    registry = TransactionAuthorizationRegistry()
    registry.register(approved)

    consumer = TransactionAuthorizationConsumer(registry)

    wrong_transaction = CanonicalTransaction.from_mapping(
        transaction_id="different",
        principal_id=authorization.transaction.principal_id,
        amount=authorization.transaction.amount,
        currency=authorization.transaction.currency,
        merchant_or_service=authorization.transaction.merchant_or_service,
        operation=authorization.transaction.operation,
        timestamp=authorization.transaction.timestamp,
        nonce="different-nonce",
    )

    result = consumer.consume_once(
        authorization.authorization_id,
        expected_transaction=wrong_transaction,
        clock=clock,
        required_assurance_level=AuthenticationAssuranceLevel.A2,
    )

    assert result.decision is TransactionAuthorizationDecision.DENY
    assert result.failure is TransactionAuthorizationFailure.INVALID_TRANSACTION_BINDING

class FixedClock:
    def __init__(self, value: datetime) -> None:
        self.value = value

    def now(self) -> datetime:
        return self.value


def make_principal(
    user_id: str = "user-001",
) -> Principal:
    return Principal(
        user_id=user_id,
        email=f"{user_id}@example.com",
        email_verified=True,
        account_status=AccountStatus.ACTIVE,
        roles=frozenset(),
    )


def make_transaction(
    now: datetime,
) -> CanonicalTransaction:
    return CanonicalTransaction.from_mapping(
        transaction_id="tx-001",
        principal_id="user-001",
        amount="100.00",
        currency="EUR",
        merchant_or_service="merchant.example",
        operation="purchase",
        timestamp=now,
        nonce="nonce-001",
        risk_context={
            "channel": "web",
            "risk": "medium",
        },
    )


def make_assurance(
    *,
    principal_id: str = "user-001",
    level: AuthenticationAssuranceLevel = (
        AuthenticationAssuranceLevel.A2
    ),
    assurance_time: datetime,
) -> AuthenticationAssuranceContext:
    return AuthenticationAssuranceContext(
        principal_id=principal_id,
        assurance_level=level,
        authentication_time=assurance_time,
        assurance_time=assurance_time,
        authentication_method="test",
        authentication_strength="mfa",
        user_verified=True,
        phishing_resistant=(
            level is AuthenticationAssuranceLevel.A3
        ),
        issuer="test",
        subject=principal_id,
        audience="easychatbot",
        evidence_id="assurance-001",
        policy_version="test-v1",
    )


def make_service() -> TransactionAuthorizationApplicationService:
    registry = TransactionAuthorizationRegistry()

    return TransactionAuthorizationApplicationService(
        authorization_service=AuthorizationService(),
        registry=registry,
        consumer=TransactionAuthorizationConsumer(registry),
    )


def make_pending_authorization(
    *,
    service: TransactionAuthorizationApplicationService,

    transaction: CanonicalTransaction,
    now: datetime,
) -> object:
    return service.create_pending_authorization(
        principal=principal,
        transaction=transaction,
        authorization_id="auth-001",
        created_at=now,
        expires_at=now + timedelta(minutes=5),
    )

    now = datetime(

    with TRANSACTION_AUTHORIZATION_SOURCE.open(
        encoding="utf-8",
    ) as handle:
        source = handle.read()

    forbidden = (
        "zitadel",
        "keycloak",
        "webauthn",
        "passkey",
        "oidc",
        "saml",
    )

    lowered = source.lower()

    for value in forbidden:
        assert value not in lowered


def test_service_does_not_implement_mfa_or_freshness_policy() -> None:
    with TRANSACTION_AUTHORIZATION_SOURCE.open(
        encoding="utf-8",
    ) as handle:
        source = handle.read().lower()

    assert "totp" not in source
    assert "otp_secret" not in source
    assert "webauthn" not in source
    assert "maximum_age" not in source
    assert (
        "authentication_time + timedelta"
        not in source
    )

def make_principal(
    *,
    roles: frozenset[str],
) -> Principal:
    return Principal(

        email_verified=True,
        account_status=AccountStatus.ACTIVE,
        roles=roles,
    )


def test_beta_user_does_not_have_functionality_control_permission():
    principal = make_principal(
        roles=frozenset({"beta_user"}),
    )

    dependency = require_permission(
        Permission.FUNCTIONALITY_CONTROL,
    )

    application = FastAPI()

    @application.get("/test")
    async def protected(
        _: Principal = Depends(dependency),
    ):
        return {"ok": True}

    # Override the identity dependency, not the permission dependency.
    #
    # This preserves the real authorization path:
    #
    # get_current_principal
    #       -> require_permission(...)
    #       -> AuthorizationService
    #       -> PermissionDeniedError
    #       -> HTTP 403
    application.dependency_overrides[
        get_current_principal
    ] = lambda: principal

    with TestClient(application) as client:
        response = client.get("/test")

    assert response.status_code == 403


def test_operator_has_functionality_control_permission():
    principal = make_principal(
        roles=frozenset({"operator"}),
    )

    dependency = require_permission(
        Permission.FUNCTIONALITY_CONTROL,
    )

    application = FastAPI()

    @application.get("/test")
    async def protected(
        _: Principal = Depends(dependency),
    ):
        return {"ok": True}

    # Override only identity so that the real authorization
    # service evaluates the operator's permission.
    application.dependency_overrides[
        get_current_principal
    ] = lambda: principal

    with TestClient(application) as client:
        response = client.get("/test")

    assert response.status_code == 200


def test_project_control_router_uses_functionality_control_permission():
    router = make_router()

    routes = [
        route
        for route in router.routes
        if hasattr(route, "path")
        and route.path
        == "/project-control/projects/{project_id}"
    ]

    assert len(routes) == 1

    route = routes[0]

    assert route.methods == {"GET"}

    dependency_calls = {
        dependency.call
        for dependency in route.dependant.dependencies
    }

    assert len(dependency_calls) == 1

    permission_dependency = next(
        iter(dependency_calls)
    )

    assert permission_dependency is not None

def build_request(
    service: AsyncMock,
    *,
    headers: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    client_host: str = "127.0.0.1",
    cookies: str | None = None,
) -> Request:
    app = SimpleNamespace(
        state=SimpleNamespace(authentication_service=service)
    )

    scope = {
        "type": "http",
        "app": app,
        "method": "POST",
        "path": "/auth/test",
        "headers": [
            (key.lower().encode(), value.encode())
            for key, value in (headers or {}).items()
        ],
        "client": (client_host, 12345),
        "scheme": "https",
        "server": ("testserver", 443),
        "query_string": b"",
        "root_path": "",
        "http_version": "1.1",
    }

    if cookies is not None:
        scope["headers"].append((b"cookie", cookies.encode()))

    return Request(scope)


def build_principal(*, is_active: bool = True) -> Principal:
    # The route only consumes the public `is_active` contract.
    return SimpleNamespace(is_active=is_active)  # type: ignore[return-value]

async def test_register_delegates_to_composed_authentication_service() -> None:
    service = AsyncMock()

        "Registration successful. Email verification is required."
    )
    service.register.assert_awaited_once_with(

    )

        session_id=session_id,

    )

        service,
        headers={"user-agent": "EasyChatBot-Test/1.0"},
        client_host="192.0.2.10",
    )
    response = Response()

    result = await login(
        LoginRequest(

            password="Strong-password-123!",
        ),
        http_request,
        response,
    )

    assert result.detail == "Login successful."
    assert result.expires_at == expires_at.isoformat()

    service.authenticate.assert_awaited_once_with(
        email="USER@example.com",
        password="Strong-password-123!",
        device_name="EasyChatBot-Test/1.0",
        ip_address="192.0.2.10",
    )

    cookie = response.headers["set-cookie"]
    assert f"easychatbot_session={session_id}" in cookie
    assert "HttpOnly" in cookie
    assert "Secure" in cookie
    assert "SameSite=lax" in cookie
    assert "Path=/" in cookie

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from app.application.identity.authentication_email_service import (
    AuthenticationEmailService,
)


class StubAuthenticationEmailSender:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.calls: list[tuple[str, dict]] = []

    async def send(
        self,
        subject: str,
        content: dict,
    ) -> dict:
        self.calls.append((subject, content))
        return {
            "provider": "stub",
            "status": "accepted",
        }


def build_service(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
    tmp_path: Path,
    *,
    privacy_url: str | None = None,
) -> tuple[AuthenticationEmailService, StubAuthenticationEmailSender]:
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        "app.application.identity.authentication_email_service."
        "_registration_email_sender",
        lambda: "EasyChatBot <noreply@example.com>",
    )

    logo_path = tmp_path / "easychatbot-logo.png"
    logo_path.write_bytes(b"fake-logo")

    sender = StubAuthenticationEmailSender()

    service = AuthenticationEmailService(
        sender,
        frontend_base_url="https://academy.example.com/",
        privacy_url=privacy_url,
        logo_path=logo_path,
    )

    return service, sender


@pytest.mark.asyncio

    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
    tmp_path: Path,
) -> None:
    service, sender = build_service(
        monkeypatch,
        tmp_path,
        privacy_url="https://academy.example.com/privacy",
    )

        verification_token="test-token",
    )

    assert result == {
        "provider": "stub",
        "status": "accepted",
    }

    assert len(sender.calls) == 1

    _, content = sender.calls[0]

    assert content["recipient"] == "user@example.com"
    assert "https://academy.example.com/privacy" in content["html"]
    assert "https://academy.example.com/privacy" in content["body"]
    assert "Data Protection" in content["html"]

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from app.application.identity.authentication_email_service import (
    AuthenticationEmailService,
)


class RecordingSender:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.calls: list[tuple[str, dict]] = []

    async def send(self, subject: str, content: dict) -> dict:
        self.calls.append((subject, content))
        return {"status": "sent"}


def build_service(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
    tmp_path: Path,
) -> tuple[AuthenticationEmailService, RecordingSender]:
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        "app.application.identity.authentication_email_service._registration_email_sender",
        lambda: "academy@easychatbotacademy.com",
    )

    logo_path = tmp_path / "easychatbot-logo.png"
    logo_path.write_bytes(b"logo")

    sender = RecordingSender()

    service = AuthenticationEmailService(
        sender,
        frontend_base_url="https://academy.example.com/",
        privacy_url="https://academy.example.com/privacy",
        logo_path=logo_path,
    )

    return service, sender

    assert expected_url in content["body"]

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime
from unittest.mock import AsyncMock
from uuid import UUID, uuid4

import pytest

from app.application.identity.authentication_service import (
    AuthenticationError,
    AuthenticationService,
)


@dataclass
class FakeUser:
    id: UUID
    email: str
    username: str


class FakeAuthenticationRepository:
    """Minimal repository contract required by authentication tests."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.created_user = None
        self.created_password = None
        self.created_verification = None
        self.email_verified = False

        self.user_by_email: FakeUser | None = None

        self.recent_password_reset_tokens = 0
        self.created_password_reset_token = None

        self.reset_password_call = None
        self.reset_password_result = True
        self.password_credential_hash = "hashed:Previous-Password-2025!"

    async def email_exists(self, email: str) -> bool:
        return False

    async def username_exists(self, username: str) -> bool:
        return False

    async def create_user(
        self,
        *,
        user_id: UUID,
        email: str,
        username: str,
    ) -> UUID:
        self.created_user = {
            "user_id": user_id,
            "email": email,
            "username": username,
        }
        return user_id

    async def create_password_credential(
        self,
        *,
        user_id: UUID,
        password_hash: str,
    ) -> None:
        self.created_password = {
            "user_id": user_id,
            "password_hash": password_hash,
        }

    async def create_email_verification(
        self,
        *,
        user_id: UUID,
        email: str,
    ) -> str:
        self.created_verification = {
            "user_id": user_id,
            "email": email,
        }
        return "raw-verification-token"

    async def get_user_by_email(
        self,
        email: str,
    ) -> FakeUser | None:
        if self.user_by_email is None:
            return None

        if self.user_by_email.email != email:
            return None

        return self.user_by_email

    async def count_recent_password_reset_tokens(
        self,
        *,
        user_id: UUID,
        since: datetime,
    ) -> int:
        return self.recent_password_reset_tokens

    async def create_password_reset_token(
        self,
        *,
        user_id: UUID,
    ) -> str:
        self.created_password_reset_token = {
            "user_id": user_id,
        }
        return "raw-password-reset-token"

    async def get_password_reset_user(
        self,
        token: str,
    ) -> FakeUser | None:
        if self.user_by_email is not None:
            return self.user_by_email
        return FakeUser(
            id=uuid4(),
            email="user@example.com",
            username="testuser",
        )

    async def get_password_reset_context(
        self,
        *,
        token: str,
    ):
        """Return the internal reset context expected by AuthenticationService."""
        user = await self.get_password_reset_user(token)
        if user is None:
            return None
        return type(
            "FakePasswordResetContext",
            (),
            {
                "user_id": user.id,
                "email": user.email,
                "password_hash": self.password_credential_hash,
            },
        )()

    async def get_password_credential(
        self,
        user_id: UUID,
    ):
        return type(
            "FakeCredential",
            (),
            {
                "user_id": user_id,
                "password_hash": self.password_credential_hash,
                "credential_type": "PASSWORD",
            },
        )()

    async def reset_password(
        self,
        *,
        token: str,
        password_hash: str,
        expected_password_hash: str | None = None,
    ) -> bool:
        self.reset_password_call = {
            "token": token,
            "password_hash": password_hash,
            "expected_password_hash": expected_password_hash,
        }
        return self.reset_password_result


class FakePasswordHasher:
    def hash(self, password: str) -> str:
        return f"hashed:{password}"

    def verify(self, password: str, encoded: str) -> bool:
        return password == encoded.removeprefix("hashed:")


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_register_creates_unverified_user_and_sends_verification_email():
    repository = FakeAuthenticationRepository()
    email_service = AsyncMock()

    service = AuthenticationService(
        repository,
        email_service=email_service,
        password_hasher=FakePasswordHasher(),
    )

    user_id = await service.register(
        email=" USER@example.com ",
        username=" testuser ",
        password="Strong-password-123!",
    )

    assert isinstance(user_id, UUID)

    assert repository.created_user == {
        "user_id": user_id,
        "email": "user@example.com",
        "username": "testuser",
    }

    assert repository.created_password == {
        "user_id": user_id,
        "password_hash": "hashed:Strong-password-123!",
    }

    assert repository.created_verification == {
        "user_id": user_id,
        "email": "user@example.com",
    }

    assert repository.email_verified is False

    email_service.send_verification_email.assert_awaited_once_with(
        email="user@example.com",
        username="testuser",
        verification_token="raw-verification-token",
    )

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest

from app.infrastructure.email.authentication_email_sender import (
    AuthenticationEmailSenderAdapter,
)


class StubEmailProviderManager:
    def __init__(self, result: dict) -> None:
        self.result = result
        self.calls: list[tuple[str, dict]] = []

    async def send(
        self,
        subject: str,
        content: dict,
    ) -> dict:
        self.calls.append((subject, content))
        return self.result


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_send_delegates_to_shared_provider_manager() -> None:
    provider_manager = StubEmailProviderManager(
        {
            "provider": "resend",
            "status": "accepted",
            "message_id": "msg_123",
        }
    )
    adapter = AuthenticationEmailSenderAdapter(
        provider_manager=provider_manager,
    )

    content = {
        "recipient": "user@example.com",
        "email_type": "authentication_verification",
        "from": "EasyChatBot <noreply@example.com>",
        "body": "Verify your email.",
        "html": "<p>Verify your email.</p>",
    }

    result = await adapter.send(
        "Verify your EasyChatBot email",
        content,
    )

    assert result == {
        "provider": "resend",
        "status": "accepted",
        "message_id": "msg_123",
    }
    assert provider_manager.calls == [
        (
            "Verify your EasyChatBot email",
            content,
        )
    ]


@pytest.mark.asyncio
